title: Dhamaal 4 Trailer Is Pure Chaos. Ajay Devgn's Gang Is Back, and This Time They Crashed a Theme Park to Tell You About It.
excerpt: Indra Kumar reunites the franchise's beloved idiots for one more treasure hunt — and after blinking first in a release-date standoff with Alpha, the laughter riot locks July 10 with a 60-foot poster unveiled at a waterfall.
body:
The trailer dropped, and within seconds you know exactly what you're getting: a screaming pile-up of men who have never once made a sensible decision, chasing a fortune that will absolutely ruin all of them. **Dhamaal 4** doesn't reinvent anything. It doesn't want to. It wants you in a packed theatre on a Friday night, popcorn in hand, laughing at **Arshad Warsi** doing something monumentally stupid. And honestly? After a year this heavy, that sounds perfect.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=IG-eByZdz6Y</youtube>

Let's start with the spectacle, because the makers clearly decided subtlety was for other people. The trailer launch was staged at **Imagicaa**, the theme park transformed to match the film's madcap treasure-hunt world, with a 60-foot poster unveiled at a grand waterfall. A waterfall. For a comedy trailer. This is the kind of unhinged commitment to bigness that the *Dhamaal* franchise has always run on, and if you're going to sell slapstick, you might as well sell it at full volume.


![Ajay Devgn — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9d/Ajay_Devgn_at_the_trailer_launch_of_Raid_2.jpg)



> **""July 10 is apt for their film," a trade source told **Bollywood Hungama**, and the fans get the comic caper a week earlier as a bonus."**



> The gang is back — older, no wiser, and racing each other to a fortune none of them deserve.

The trailer itself is exactly the controlled demolition fans wanted. **Ajay Devgn** anchors the chaos with that signature deadpan, the still center around which everyone else loses their minds. **Arshad Warsi**, **Riteish Deshmukh**, **Jaaved Jaaferi** and **Sanjay Mishra** slot back into the rhythm like no time has passed — the comic timing between them is the franchise's real special effect. The setup is franchise canon: a massive fortune surfaces, the gang catches wind, and what follows is a no-holds-barred race driven by rivalry, greed, and pure dumb luck. Misunderstandings stack on misunderstandings. Nobody trusts anybody. Everybody is trying to outsmart everybody else, and everybody is bad at it.

Joining the circus this round is a deep ensemble — **Esha Gupta**, **Sanjeeda Shaikh**, **Anjali Anand**, **Upendra Limaye**, **Vijay Patkar** and the gloriously loud **Ravi Kishan**. Director **Indra Kumar**, who has shepherded this series since the 2007 original, knows precisely what tonal lane he's in. *Total Dhamaal* (2019) pulled in over ₹150 crore by leaning all the way into family-friendly mayhem, and there's no reason to believe Kumar has suddenly discovered restraint.


![Theme Park — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/%ED%8F%AC%EC%8B%9C%EC%A6%8C%EC%8A%A4_%EC%82%B0%EB%A6%AC%EC%98%A4%EB%8C%84%EC%8A%A4%ED%83%80%EC%9E%84_2025.jpg/3840px-%ED%8F%AC%EC%8B%9C%EC%A6%8C%EC%8A%A4_%EC%82%B0%EB%A6%AC%EC%98%A4%EB%8C%84%EC%8A%A4%ED%83%80%EC%9E%84_2025.jpg)


The more delicious story, though, is the one that played out off-screen — a release-date game of chicken between two of the summer's biggest titles. *Dhamaal 4* was originally booked for July 17. Then **YRF's Alpha** — the Alia Bhatt and Sharvari spy thriller — was eyeing the same window, so *Dhamaal 4* preponed to July 10 to dodge the clash. Then *Alpha* blinked and jumped all the way to July 3, leaving July 10 wide open. The *Dhamaal 4* team, having already moved, simply planted their flag and stayed. "July 10 is apt for their film," a trade source told **Bollywood Hungama**, and the fans get the comic caper a week earlier as a bonus. Two heavyweight productions doing an elaborate scheduling tango, and the comedy franchise walked away with the better date.

What it all sets up is a genuinely stacked four-week stretch at the box office. **Cocktail 2** pours out June 19, **Welcome to the Jungle** swings in June 26, **Alpha** lands July 3, and **Dhamaal 4** closes the run July 10. Four consecutive Fridays, four very different appetites — sexy ensemble romance, nostalgia comedy, female-led spy spectacle, and pure slapstick. For diaspora audiences mapping out summer cinema runs, that's a full month of reasons to make the drive to the multiplex.

For NRIs in the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf, *Dhamaal* has always been comfort food — the kind of broad, language-no-bar comedy that plays just as well to a multi-generational living room as it does to a sold-out Friday crowd. Expect the standard wide overseas theatrical rollout from a Maddock-scale tentpole, with a streaming landing on a major OTT platform to follow some weeks after the cinema run, in the franchise's usual fashion.

Is it going to win anyone an award? Of course not. Is it going to be the loudest, dumbest, most cathartic two hours in a theatre this July? The trailer is betting its entire 60-foot, waterfall-backed budget that yes. And against a summer this serious, sometimes the gang of idiots is exactly the medicine you didn't know you needed.
